claims.text: Machine-learning algorithms can predict optimal refractory high-entropy alloy compositions.
Machine-learning-designed RHEAs will have greater strength than RHEAs designed by traditional methods.
Machine-learning-designed RHEAs will have greater ductility than RHEAs designed by traditional methods.
Machine-learning-designed RHEAs will maintain lower weight than RHEAs designed by traditional methods.
Existing RHEAs have varying compositions and properties.
The proposed machine-learning model is trained using known RHEA compositions and their corresponding mechanical properties.
Specific elemental compositions influence the microstructural characteristics of RHEAs.
Machine-learning algorithms can identify complex relationships between RHEA composition and mechanical properties.
Identifying composition–property relationships enables prediction of compositions that jointly optimize strength and ductility.
Predicted RHEA compositions will exhibit a statistically significant increase in strength relative to traditionally designed compositions.
Predicted RHEA compositions will exhibit a statistically significant increase in ductility relative to traditionally designed compositions.
Predicted RHEA compositions will have lower density than traditionally designed compositions.
The effectiveness of machine learning for RHEA composition design depends on the quality and quantity of available training data.
The proposed hypothesis applies only to refractory high-entropy alloys.
